subject: music
topicDisplay: Area of Study 6: Music for Small Ensemble
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which instruments make up a standard string quartet?
options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.explain: A string quartet consists of first violin, second violin, viola and cello.

questions.q: A piano trio typically consists of which instruments?
questions.explain: The classical piano trio combines piano with violin and cello.

questions.q: Which group of instruments usually forms the rhythm section of a jazz combo?
questions.explain: The rhythm section provides harmony and pulse, typically using piano, double bass and drums.

questions.q: A defining feature of chamber music is that:
options: each part is played by a single performer
it is written only for full orchestra
every instrument plays the same line
questions.explain: Chamber music is written for a small ensemble with one player to a part.

questions.q: A standard wind quintet is made up of:
options: flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon and horn
two flutes, oboe, clarinet and bassoon
flute, oboe, clarinet, trumpet and horn
flute, clarinet, saxophone, bassoon and horn
questions.explain: The woodwind quintet pairs four woodwinds with a French horn.

questions.q: The 12-bar blues is built mainly on which three chords?
questions.explain: The 12-bar blues uses the tonic (I), subdominant (IV) and dominant (V) chords.

questions.q: When one instrument plays a phrase that is answered by another, this interplay is called:
questions.explain: Call and response, or antiphony, alternates musical phrases between performers.

questions.q: In jazz, improvised wordless vocal singing on nonsense syllables is known as:
questions.explain: Scat singing is improvised vocal melody sung on nonsense syllables.

questions.q: Chamber ensembles usually perform without a conductor because:
options: the small number of players can lead and listen to one another directly
the music is too simple to need one
conductors are not permitted in chamber music
the players cannot see a conductor
questions.explain: With few players, performers coordinate by listening and watching each other rather than a conductor.

questions.q: A texture with a clear melody supported by chordal accompaniment is described as:
questions.explain: Homophonic texture combines a main melody with harmonic accompaniment.

questions.q: When two or more independent melodic lines sound at the same time, the texture is:
questions.explain: Polyphonic or contrapuntal texture weaves several independent melodic lines together.

questions.q: In a jazz performance, the term 'head' refers to:
options: the main tune or theme stated at the start and end
questions.explain: The head is the principal melody played before and after the improvised solos.

questions.q: When a pianist or guitarist plays supporting chords behind a soloist, this is known as:
questions.explain: Comping is the improvised chordal accompaniment that supports a soloist.

questions.q: The front line of a jazz combo generally:
options: plays the melodies and takes the solos
keeps only the beat and harmony
consists of piano, bass and drums
questions.explain: Front-line instruments such as trumpet and saxophone carry the melody and improvise solos.

questions.q: In imitation, a melodic idea is:
options: introduced by one part and then copied by another
played by all parts in unison
questions.explain: Imitation occurs when one voice states a phrase that another voice then echoes.

questions.q: A walking bass line is best described as:
options: a steady line of mostly even notes moving stepwise or by small leaps
a series of loud accented chords
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even notes, usually one per beat, outlining the harmony.

questions.q: A jazz standard has four eight-bar sections in which the third contrasts with the others. This 32-bar structure is:
questions.explain: The AABA form has a contrasting bridge (B) as its third eight-bar section.

questions.q: A saxophone plays a four-bar solo, immediately answered by a four-bar drum solo, alternating back and forth. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Trading fours is the exchange of four-bar improvised solos between players.

questions.q: In a passage, all the instruments play exactly the same melody with no harmony. The texture is:
questions.explain: A single melodic line, even doubled in unison, produces a monophonic texture.

questions.q: An ensemble of flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon and French horn plays chamber music. This group is a:
questions.explain: These five instruments make up the standard wind (woodwind) quintet.
